explanation: The common cuckoo chick usually hatches early and pushes the host's eggs out of the nest. Its foster parents keep feeding it even after it dwarfs them.

claims.text: The common cuckoo lays its eggs in the nests of other bird species, which raise its chick.
Magpies, starlings and swallows raise their own chicks rather than laying eggs in other species' nests.
A newly hatched common cuckoo chick often pushes the host's eggs or chicks out of the nest.
Host parents keep feeding the cuckoo chick even when it grows much larger than they are.
